title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: In an agent, as opposed to a workflow, what decides which step happens next?

options.text: The model decides at run time, based on what it has seen so far
The programmer's code fixes the order of the steps before the program runs
The user approves each step before the program moves on to the next one
The model decides, but only from a fixed script written beforehand

items.stem: Every booking request in your assistant runs the same code path: check_calendar, then book_machine if free, then send a confirmation. The model only fills in the machine and date. What is this?

options.text: An agent, because it calls tools and uses a language model
A workflow, because the code fixes the steps and their order
An agent, because the model fills in the tool arguments
A workflow, because the model never sees any tool results

items.stem: A program sends each question to the model once to label it "manual" or "booking", then runs fixed code for that label. Who decides the next step after the label, and why is this a workflow?
A fixed workflow makes exactly 2 model calls per request. An agent on the same requests averages 6 model calls. Each call costs the same. How many times more does the agent cost per request?
Manual questions vary: some need one page, others need several searches across machines, and you cannot know how many beforehand. Which design fits these questions best?

options.text: A workflow with three fixed searches, since every question needs similar work
A workflow with one search, since most questions need one page
A workflow that asks the student to pick each search by hand
An agent, since the number of searches depends on what each returns

items.stem: Booking steps are known, and a wrong booking is costly. Manual lookup needs an unknown number of searches. Which design is the best argument at your design review?

options.text: One agent for both, with a human confirming each booking
One workflow for everything, so the cost stays fully predictable
A fixed workflow for booking and an agent for manual lookup
An agent for booking and a fixed workflow for manual lookup
